title: Administrative-scale evidence translated into corridor questions
rule: These observations calibrate questions and service interfaces only. They are not spatial allocations, corridor baselines, performance targets, or official planning controls.

records.design_translation: Prioritise standard assurance, failure records, rights/IP and public-service interfaces across the three nodes instead of claiming a generic incubator or inventing corridor capacity.
records.not_inferred: These totals do not locate resources inside the Jing-Zhang corridor, prove participation, or set a project target.

records.design_translation: Use only as a scale check for the innovation narrative; keep the proposal focused on verifiable service quality, public accountability and reuse rather than rankings.
records.not_inferred: Administrative definitions and institutional coverage are not assumed to be directly comparable with Haidian or the corridor.

records.design_translation: Keep rail transfer, walking and cycling as the first public interface; test the last 300–800 metres with a small, time-bounded and reversible window before any event or route expansion.
records.not_inferred: These city-level figures do not provide station-level OD, crossing safety, parking demand, route capacity or a Jing-Zhang baseline.

records.design_translation: Make the AI Origin Community a proposed conversion clinic for laboratory safety, rights/IP, asset operation and results transfer, with appointment and paper/ human alternatives.
records.not_inferred: One event does not prove that all 37 universities share the same demand, have agreed to participate, or define a spatial service volume.
